title: 34. Influence of activity and mounting behavior of feedlot steers on complete blood cell analysis metrics.
content:
Abstract
Immune function is associated with variation in temperament. Our objective was to determine if there are health profile differences between animals with high activity and those with low activity in a feedlot setting. We hypothesize that animals with higher activity will have variation in white blood cell counts when compared to calmer animals. Yearling crossbred steers (n = 100) were fitted with 701x ear tags to monitor steps and mounting behavior in a feedlot setting. At the beginning of the study, mid-study, and end of the study blood samples were collected for complete blood count (CBC) analysis. Activity metrics included: mean daily steps, mean beats per minute, mean daily seconds walking, total seconds walking, total distance, and mean daily distance. Mounting metrics included total mounts. The Reg procedure of SAS was utilized to regress activity, mounting, and date on CBC metrics. The regression model was significant for white blood cell (WBC; P < 0.0001; R2=0.17) and neutrophil number (NeuNum; P < 0.0001; R2=0.10) where activity (0.06, P < 0.0001; 0.06, P < 0.0001) and date (-0.02, P = 0.003; 0.0006, P = 0.0003) were significant predictors yet mounting was not (P = 0.58). Similarly, the model was significant for mean platelet volume (MPV; P < 0.001; R2=0.11) with activity and date as significant predictors, however, while activity had a positive coefficient (0.02, P = 0.02), date also positively influenced the model (0.004, P < 0.0001). The model was also significant for lymphocyte number (LymNum; P < 0.0001; R2=0.15), monocyte number (MonNum; P < 0.0001; R2=0.08), eosin percentage (EosPerc; P = 0.03; R2 =0.03), red blood cell (RBC; P < 0.01; R2=0.05), mean corpuscular volume (MCV; P < 0.0001; R2=0.30), mean corpuscular hemoglobin (MCH; P < 0.0001; R2=0.22), mean corpuscular hemoglobin concentration (MCHC; P < 0.0001; R2=0.16), red cell distribution width-coefficient of variation (RDWCV; P < 0.0001; R2=0.50), and platelet (PLT; P = 0.005; R2=0.04), yet date was the only significant predictor (P ≤ 0.005). The coefficient for date was negative (-0.66 – -0.0011) for LymNum, MonNum, RBC, MCHC, RDWCV, and PLT and positive (0.007 – 0.05) for EosPerc, MCV, and MCH. When represented as a percentage, neutrophils (P = 0.0001; R2=0.07) and lymphocytes (P = 0.0002; R2=0.06) were significantly predicted by activity (0.43, P < 0.001; -0.47, P = 0.0001) but not by mounting or date (P ≥ 0.54). Lastly, the model was significant for hemoglobin (P < 0.0001; R2=0.12) and hematocrit (P < 0.0001; R2=0.18) where mounting (0.002, P = 0.0012; 0.007, P = 0.0006) and date (0.007, P < 0.0001; 0.03, P < 0.0001) were significant predictors, yet activity was not (P ≥ 0.61). Date had the largest influence indicating that CBC metrics are dynamic. Activity influenced WBC but not RBC metrics where the opposite was true with mounting except for MPV for activity. Activity and mounting influence blood characteristics differently, yet the biological relevance of these changes is unknown and needs further characterization.
